web.title: UX Design Patterns for Loading - Pencil & Paper
web.description:
# Loading Feedback
## Loading patterns
### Between 0.1 and 1 second
Make sure you do not try to “fill that time” with a spinner or an animation.

### Above 1 second
#### Skeleton loader screen
**Optional:** Shimmer effect (by Facebook)

An equally effective animation device is pulsing.

## Wrapping up
The key thing to keep in mind is that loading states give users visibility on the system status. To decide on the best way to do that, you need to take into account the way your data is structured, the context of your user’s workflow, and the perceived value of the task being executed.

web.title: Skeleton Screens vs Loading Spinners: When to Use Each
AI Loading States - UX Patterns
web.description:
## Use Cases ### Choose the right pattern [Streaming Response](https://uxpatterns.dev/patterns/ai-intelligence/streaming-response) Choose when users need streaming response instead of ai loading states as the primary interaction Why it wins Clearer fit for its own job, Lower ambiguity about the expected interaction Tradeoffs Less specialized for ai loading states, Different states and recovery paths to teach Read pattern [Loading Indicator](https://uxpatterns.dev/patterns/user-feedback/loading-indicator) Choose when users need loading indicator instead of ai loading states as the primary interaction Why it wins Clearer fit for its own job, Lower ambiguity about the expected interaction Tradeoffs Less specialized for ai loading states, Different states and recovery paths to teach Read pattern [Skeleton](https://uxpatterns.dev/patterns/user-feedback/skeleton) Choose when users need skeleton instead of ai loading states as the primary interaction Why it wins Clearer fit for its own job, Lower ambiguity about the expected interaction Tradeoffs Less specialized for ai loading states, Different states and recovery paths to teach Read pattern ## Benefits - Clarifies how ai loading states should behave before implementation details begin to sprawl. ## Anatomy AI Loading States Request state Streaming placeholder Status label Fallback state ## Best Practices ### Accessibility - Verify that ai loading states can be completed using keyboard alone. - Keep focus order logical when the pattern opens, updates, or reveals additional UI. - Preserve a visible focus state that is still readable at high zoom. - Use semantic elements first, then add ARIA only where semantics alone are not enough. - Announce state changes such as errors, loading, or completion in the right place and with the right politeness. ### Visual Design - Separate system status from generated content visually. - Keep request, streaming, and completion states recognizable at a glance. - Use subtle motion to show progress without distracting from reading. ## Examples ### Basic Implementation ```html

AI Loading States

Basic demo placeholder for loading states for ai operations.

``` ### What this example demonstrates - A clear baseline implementation of ai loading states that can be reviewed without framework-specific noise. ## Frequently Asked Questions When should I choose AI Loading States instead of Streaming Response? Choose ai loading states when the job depends on communicate request progress, streaming readiness, and intermediate AI work without pretending to know the exact finish time. If the team only needs a lighter interaction with fewer states, Streaming Response will usually be easier to ship and maintain. The biggest risk is usually not the default visual state. It is the combination of state management, accessibility, and recovery behavior once loading, errors, or narrow screens enter the picture. How do I know whether ai loading states is working well? Watch whether users can complete the intended job without pausing to decode the interface, whether state changes feel trustworthy, and whether edge cases behave as intentionally as the happy path. ## Related Patterns [**Streaming Response**\ \ Learn how to implement streaming AI responses. Discover best practices for progressive rendering, markdown formatting, and stream interruption.](https://uxpatterns.dev/patterns/ai-intelligence/streaming-response) [**Loading Indicator**\ \ Build effective loading indicators for your web applications. Learn best practices for implementing loading states, spinners, and progress feedback with proper accessibility.](https://uxpatterns.dev/patterns/user-feedback/loading-indicator) [**Skeleton**\ \ Build effective skeleton loading states for your web applications. Learn best practices for implementing content placeholders and loading animations with proper accessibility.](https://uxpatterns.dev/patterns/user-feedback/skeleton)
